title: pH and Kw; Ka, pKa and Kb; pH of weak acids/bases; salt hydrolysis; Neutralization and salts
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: AB02#t3 term and clue written for the game; AB02#t2 term and clue written for the game; AB02#t1 term and clue written for the game; AB05#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: AB02#N.4, AB04#N.4, AB05#N.5, AB06#N.3b, AB02#N.10b, AB04#N.10, AB05#N.6, AB06#N.4, AB02#N.12, AB04#N.13, AB05#N.10, AB06#N.9.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Neutral solution
items.clue: An aqueous mixture in which [H⁺] equals [OH⁻].

items.label: Universal indicator
items.clue: Paper or liquid matched against a chart to estimate pH to about 1 unit.

items.label: pH meter
items.clue: Gives a precise reading, usually to 0.01, after being calibrated with buffers.

items.label: Ka
items.clue: Equilibrium constant for the dissociation of a weak acid, with water left out.

questions.stem: Hydrobromic acid, HBr, is a strong acid. What is the pH of 4.0 × 10⁻³ M HBr(aq)?
questions.explanation: HBr ionises completely, so [H⁺] = 4.0 × 10⁻³ and pH = −log₁₀(4.0 × 10⁻³) = 2.40.

questions.stem: Which reaction produces a salt and water, with no other product?

options.text: Potassium carbonate with hydrochloric acid
Ammonia with sulfuric acid
Barium hydroxide with nitric acid
Zinc with hydrochloric acid

questions.explanation: Each OH⁻ takes one H⁺ to form water: Ba(OH)₂ + 2HNO₃ → Ba(NO₃)₂ + 2H₂O.

questions.stem: Benzoic acid has pKa = 4.20. What is its Ka?
questions.explanation: Ka = 10⁻⁴·²⁰ = 6.3 × 10⁻⁵. Sense check: pKa between 4 and 5, so Ka between 10⁻⁵ and 10⁻⁴.

questions.stem: A 0.10 M solution of a weak monoprotic acid, HA, is prepared at 25°C. The pKa of HA is 5.20. What is the pH of the solution?
questions.explanation: Ka = 10⁻⁵·²⁰ = 6.3 × 10⁻⁶. x² = Ka × 0.10 = 6.3 × 10⁻⁷, so x = 7.9 × 10⁻⁴ M and pH = 3.10. Less than 1% ionizes, so the approximation holds.

questions.stem: What is the pH of a 0.025 M solution of Ba(OH)₂ at 25°C?
questions.explanation: Ba(OH)₂ dissociates completely, giving [OH⁻] = 2 × 0.025 M = 0.050 M. pOH = −log(0.050) = 1.30, and pH = 14.00 − 1.30 = 12.70.

questions.stem: What are the parent acid and parent base of ammonium methanoate, HCOONH₄?

options.text: Parent acid HCOO⁻; parent base NH₄⁺
Parent acid HCOOH; parent base NH₄⁺
Parent acid NH₃; parent base HCOOH
Parent acid HCOOH; parent base NH₃

questions.explanation: The anion HCOO⁻ comes from methanoic acid; the cation NH₄⁺ formed when NH₃ accepted a proton. HCOOH + NH₃ → HCOONH₄.

questions.stem: At 25 °C the pKa of methanoic acid, HCOOH, is 3.75 and the pKa of ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH, is 4.76. Which statement about 0.10 M solutions of the two acids is correct?

options.text: Ethanoic acid is the stronger acid, as its pKa is the larger.
Both are dissociated to the same extent, as both are weak acids.
Methanoic acid needs more NaOH(aq) to neutralise the same volume of it.
Methanoic acid is dissociated to a greater extent than ethanoic acid.

questions.explanation: The smaller pKa means the larger Ka (1.8 × 10⁻⁴ against 1.7 × 10⁻⁵), so methanoic acid is stronger and more dissociated at the same concentration.

questions.stem: A 0.20 M solution of a weak acid, HA, has pH 2.70 at 25°C. What is Ka?
Two samples of rain are tested with a pH meter. Sample A has pH 4.2; sample B has pH 5.7. How does [H⁺] in sample A compare with [H⁺] in sample B?

options.text: It is 1.5 times greater, as the pH values differ by 1.5.
It is about 15 times greater: 10 times for each pH unit.
It is about 32 times greater.
It is about 32 times smaller, as sample A has the lower pH.

questions.explanation: [H⁺] = 10⁻ᵖᴴ, so the ratio is 10⁻⁴·² ÷ 10⁻⁵·⁷ = 10¹·⁵ ≈ 32. Lower pH, more H⁺.

questions.stem: At 25°C, 30.0 mL of 0.10 M HCl(aq) is mixed with 20.0 mL of 0.10 M NaOH(aq). What is the pH of the resulting solution?
questions.explanation: 3.0 mmol H₃O⁺ react with 2.0 mmol OH⁻, leaving 1.0 mmol in 50.0 mL: [H₃O⁺] = 0.020 M, so pH = −log(0.020) = 1.70.

questions.stem: A student claims that for the conjugate acid-base pair HA and A⁻, Kb = 1/Ka, because the reaction of A⁻ with water is the reverse of the ionization of HA in water. Which statement best evaluates the student's claim?

options.text: It is correct, because reversing a reaction gives the reciprocal of its K value
It is incorrect, because A⁻ + H₂O ⇌ HA + OH⁻ is not the reverse of the HA ionization
It is incorrect, because Kb equals Ka for a conjugate acid-base pair
It is incorrect, because Ka + Kb equals Kw for a conjugate acid-base pair

questions.explanation: The reverse is H₃O⁺ + A⁻ ⇌ HA + H₂O, K = 1/Ka. The base reaction is different; added to the acid ionization it gives 2H₂O ⇌ H₃O⁺ + OH⁻, so Ka × Kb = Kw.

questions.stem: A 0.10 M solution of a weak base, B, is prepared at 25°C. The pKb of B is 4.40. What is the pOH of the solution?
questions.explanation: Kb = 10⁻⁴·⁴⁰ = 4.0 × 10⁻⁵. x² = Kb × 0.10 = 4.0 × 10⁻⁶, so x = 2.0 × 10⁻³ M and pOH = 2.70. Only 2% of B ionizes.
